payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #288, slice C (split crates/brokkr-cli/src/tui.rs along its seams, with no function over CC 15 or 100 lines).

The branch story-288c-tui is on main 5eda13bf and ends at 5795d753, one commit. It comes from implement-story-288-split-the-en-3b24e74f, which shipped (chief: residual, low, no security residual). The controller's exact-coverage gate is green.

What it delivers:
- tui.rs shrinks from 3,549 lines (119 functions, summed CC 509) to 134 lines: the module doc, the imports, the constants, the mod declarations and the crate-facing re-exports. There are 12 modules under src/tui/: state, keys, movement, footer, style, panes, glyphs, layout, painter, seats, participant and terminal. Each is under 800 lines.
- Every function is at CC 15 or under (max 14). The six over 15 are split:
  - apply 23 → 14, plus read_key;
  - drive 19 → 11, plus arrive;
  - footer_for 18 → 8, plus run_footer and participant_footer;
  - from_key 17 → 4, plus from_code;
  - typed 17 → 12, plus hearth_key;
  - paint 16 → 11, plus paint_seg.
  plan and draw_participant are split under 100 lines, and their two too_many_lines expects go (production 37 → 35). Tui's struct_excessive_bools and start's too_many_arguments stay; the notes give the reason.
- Bodies are moved verbatim. The review diffed all 119 original functions: 8 declared splits and 4 rustfmt signature wraps. No trait was added (decision 0071 ruling 2).
- Two source-scanning tests (tui/source_tests.rs, and tests/boundary_readouts.rs's pair-helper pin) now read every module tui.rs declares, and refuse a declaration in any form but `mod name;`.
- All 47 .snap files are byte-identical. No test changed its name or its assertions. No baseline was raised (quality/ratchet.sh baselines).

This slice precedes #491 (the fleet view redesign), which will touch only the fleet pane's module.

Judge:
1. That the split keeps behaviour and bytes: every moved body is the original, or a declared split whose arms are the original's arms. No key binding, footer text, frame or refusal changed. The 47 snapshots and #414's focus and selection tests pass unchanged.
2. That the source-scanning tests still fail closed after the split: a Command::new, or a pair helper, in any tui module is still found, and a module declared other than `mod name;` is refused.
3. That the modules follow seams, not line counts, and that no production clone was introduced (quality/ratchet.sh clones).

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy on the crates you touched with -D warnings, typos --hidden, and quality/ratchet.sh files and clones (all clean). Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",

members.adversarial: Adversarial review of 5795d753 (#288 slice C) against 5eda13bf. The split is behaviour- and byte-preserving; I could not break it. Method: parsed every fn from the pre-change tui.rs (119) and from all 12 new production modules with a brace-depth splitter that handles `;` inside array types (estate, look, seat_texts, seat_widths), then compared bodies INCLUDING string and char literals and comments. All 119 names survive; only the 8 declared splits differ (apply/read_key, typed/hearth_key, from_key/from_code, footer_for/run_footer+participant_footer, paint/paint_seg, plan/lay, draw_participant/head_lines+checkpoint_lines+transcript_pane, drive/arrive); the other 111 bodies are exactly identical after whitespace normalisation, and every string literal and key-binding char literal across the split groups is preserved (footer text, HELP, refusals, 'q','j','k','g','G','r','/','?','[',']','1'..='9' unchanged). Structs/enums/consts/types differ only by private->pub(super); the one new type `Laid` is private and consumed by lay/plan. Signatures differ only by visibility and rustfmt wrapping; no parameter, return type or field changed. All 47 .snap files are byte-identical. Fail-closed pins verified: tests/boundary_readouts.rs::tui_sources() panics on any root `mod` line not exactly `mod name;` and reads every declared module; tui/source_tests.rs::the_tui_source_reads_every_production_module refuses any .rs file or directory under src/tui that SOURCE does not read. Runs: 139 tui lib tests pass (incl. source_tests and the #414 focus/selection tests), boundary_readouts 6/6, source_tests 1/1. Gates all hold: cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy -p brokkr-cli --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings, quality/ratchet.sh files, clones, crap (max production CC 14, no tui function over 15) and baselines 5eda13bf, typos --hidden, cargo check -p brokkr-cli --lib, cargo doc. No input->wrong output found and no source-scan bypass reachable by a realistic accident. Residual (low, non-security): the knowingly retained pre-existing architecture breach carried over unchanged by the move -- start() in tui/terminal.rs keeps 11 parameters, over the 7-parameter ceiling (decision 0071 rulings 4 and 10) and over ruling 10's parameter-object pattern, with #[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)], and Tui keeps #[expect(clippy::struct_excessive_bools)]; both moved verbatim, named with the reason in the commit (removing them would change the crate-facing entry signature/state), and carried as tracked debt. No security residual.
members.correctness: Medium (decision 0071 ruling 9): the fail-closed TUI source scans exempt every *_tests.rs file and every mod *_tests; declaration solely by suffix (tui/source_tests.rs:40; tests/boundary_readouts.rs:74). A production mod fleet_tests; without #[cfg(test)] therefore compiles a module that neither SOURCE nor the pair-helper scan reads; a Command::new or direct served.model read there escapes the claimed guard. Require the exemption to be tied to an actual test-only declaration and prove the bypass closes with a compiling mutation. Otherwise the extraction checks out: all 119 original function names remain, only the eight declared splits changed bodies, module seams are coherent, snapshots and frozen areas are untouched, and no production clone was apparent. Review was read-only; controller reported exact coverage green.

result.notes: Chief synthesis of 5795d753 (#288 slice C) on 5eda13bf. Plan's field set is unchanged; Laid is private. draw, start, production_ops and transcript_surfaces_for_test keep their old visibility. All 47 .snap files are byte-identical. Judging item 1 (behaviour and bytes) holds; item 3 (seams, no clone) holds, the modules follow the frame's order and the clone ratchet is green; item 2 (fail closed) holds for the three declared cases with one gap, finding 1. FINDINGS, deduplicated: [1] medium, correctness (decision 0071 ruling 9), CONFIRMED by my own mutation: `mod fleet_tests;` appended to tui.rs with no #[cfg(test)], and src/tui/fleet_tests.rs holding both std::process::Command::new and a part.served.model.text read: the_tui_source_reads_every_production_module PASSED, a_boxed_codex_hint_is_inert_data_and_starts_no_process PASSED and no_rust_readout_reads_the_model_cell_outside_the_pair_helper PASSED. Fix: exempt a module only when its `mod` line in tui.rs sits under #[cfg(test)], in both scans, and bind it with this exact mutation. Not carried as security: the guard is strictly stronger than the pre-split read of tui.rs alone, it is a test-time source proof, and no runtime refusal is weakened. [2] low, chief (ruling 5): which src/tui files are production is decided twice, by a directory scan in source_tests.rs and by a declaration parse in boundary_readouts.rs, each with its own copy of the suffix exemption, which is why the hole in [1] exists in two places; fold into [1]'s fix so both scans read one piece of evidence. Pre-existing tracked debt, not new to this change. No files changed, nothing committed.

Returned finding [1] (medium, ruling 9) answered in da5298dc on top of 5795d753, folding [2] (low, ruling 5): both TUI source scans now tell test modules from production by the same evidence in tui.rs, `#[cfg(test)]` on the line directly above `mod name;`, instead of the `_tests` name suffix. crates/brokkr-cli/src/tui/source_tests.rs: the directory scan exempts a file only if include_str!("../tui.rs") contains "#[cfg(test)]\nmod {stem};\n". crates/brokkr-cli/tests/boundary_readouts.rs: tui_sources() tracks the previous raw line and skips a declaration only when it is exactly #[cfg(test)]; the `mod name;`-only refusal is unchanged. Two files, +19/-8; no production code, snapshot or baseline touched. BINDING (each run this session, restored after): planted the review's exact mutation (`mod fleet_tests;` appended to tui.rs with no cfg(test); src/tui/fleet_tests.rs holding std::process::Command::new and `part.served.model.text`): the_tui_source_reads_every_production_module FAILED (left: ["fleet_tests.rs"]) and no_rust_readout_reads_the_model_cell_outside_the_pair_helper FAILED ("crates/brokkr-cli/src/tui/fleet_tests.rs:4 reads `served.model`"). With the fix reverted to HEAD's suffix rule and the mutation still planted, both passed (1/1, 6/6), which is the hole. GATES on the final tree: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy -p brokkr-cli --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean; typos --hidden clean; quality/ratchet.sh files "file size holds"; quality/ratchet.sh clones "duplication holds"; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --all-features --locked all green (lib 529 passed, every integration binary ok). Not run: cargo test --workspace (only brokkr-cli test code changed), bundle compile, and scripts/coverage-exact.sh (the controller runs it); those are pending. Both read the same declaration in tui.rs, and each doc comment names the other. Commit is GPG-signed (G) and signed off; not pushed.

members.adversarial: Adversarial review of the landing branch story-288c-tui (base 5eda13bf, HEAD da5298dc; two commits: 5795d753 the split, da5298dc the source-scan fix) against decision 0071 rulings 1, 2, 4, 5, 9 and 10. I tried to break the split and could not. Independent body diff: a brace-depth extractor (masking string and char literals) pulled 119 functions from the pre-change tui.rs and 130 from the 12 new production modules; 111 originals are byte-identical and the only unmatched bodies are exactly the 8 declared splits (apply/read_key, typed/hearth_key, from_key/from_code, footer_for/run_footer+participant_footer, paint/paint_seg, plan/lay, draw_participant/head_lines+checkpoint_lines+transcript_pane, drive/arrive). I read each split arm-for-arm: apply returns read_key for the whole reader block; typed's hearth_key returns Continue exactly where the old inner match did and otherwise falls through to the same q/j/k/g/G/r/slash/? match; footer_for's (level,pane) tuple match becomes level plus a per-level pane match with identical guards and fallbacks; from_key delegates to an identical from_code table; paint_seg reproduces marks then selection_box then name in the same order; lay's built.first() and zip over built[start..end] and phases[start..end] equal the old first()/enumerate over phases[start+index]; arrive preserves drive's order (L6 clear, classify_refresh over views.transcript, status=fresh.note, return fresh, then failures=0); draw_participant's head/checkpoint/transcript order is unchanged. A whole-file line-multiset diff accounts for every non-function item; structs/enums/consts/types differ only by private->pub(super), the one new type Laid is private and consumed by plan/lay, no parameter, return type or field changed, and no trait was added (ruling 2). 47/47 .snap files are byte-identical. Source scans fail closed: tui/source_tests.rs refuses any .rs file or non-snapshots directory under src/tui that SOURCE does not hold; boundary_readouts.rs::tui_sources() panics on any root declaration not exactly 'mod name;' and reads every declared production module. I replicated both predicates: a planted production module carrying Command::new or served.model is flagged, and 'pub(super) mod footer;', '#[path]' and 'pub mod' declarations are refused. The da5298dc fix (test-only by the #[cfg(test)] line directly above the declaration, not by name) closes the parent panel's medium: a 'mod fleet_tests;' without cfg(test) is now read by both scans. Gates run here: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy -p brokkr-cli --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings clean; typos --hidden clean; quality/ratchet.sh files ('file size holds'), clones ('duplication holds') and baselines 5eda13bf ('no baseline raised'); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib tui = 144 passed, --test boundary_readouts = 6 passed. No concrete inputs->wrong-output found, no fail-open path and no weakened refusal, so no security residual. Residual LOW (decision 0071 ruling 4, carried under ruling 10 with the implementer's stated reason): crates/brokkr-cli/src/tui/terminal.rs:246 moves start with 11 parameters, over ruling 4's 7-parameter ceiling, keeping the reason-named #[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)]; ratchet pairs a moved function with no baseline entry at its new file as new, and the signature is unchanged from the old tui.rs, so it is a moved-as-new ceiling breach rather than a new one. Tui's struct_excessive_bools at state.rs:125 is observed but not carried: ruling 4 names no bools ceiling. For the record, the branch holds two commits, not the one the commission describes; that is process, not a finding. The correctness member for this run reported clean.

result.notes: Chief synthesis of the review panel for story-288c-tui (base 5eda13bf, HEAD da5298dc, two commits: 5795d753 the seam split, da5298dc the cfg(test)-line fix). Panel: adversarial ruled residual/low, correctness ruled clean; joined result residual, so the floor is residual. Neither member's notes address the gate or argue for a lower result; nothing to rule against. Own read confirms the panel. (1) Behaviour and bytes: a normalised line-multiset diff of the old tui.rs against the root plus the 12 production modules leaves only the 8 declared splits, 5 rustfmt signature wraps (estate, run_labels, transcript_invalidates, transcript_lines, draw_participant), private->pub(super) widening, the mod/use lines and module docs. I read every split arm-for-arm: read_key is apply's reader block; hearth_key's guard is the De Morgan of typed's and its three arms return the same switch; run_footer and participant_footer are footer_for's (level,pane) arms with identical guards and fallbacks; from_code is from_key's table; paint_seg is paint's per-segment loop body with &mut cells threaded; lay's zip over built[start..end] and phases[start..end] is exact because built is mapped one-to-one from phases; arrive keeps drive's L6 clear, classify_refresh over the displayed transcript, status = fresh.note, return, then failures = 0; draw_participant keeps head/checkpoints/transcript order. Laid is private and consumed by plan only; no trait added (0071 ruling 2). All 47 .snap files unchanged (git diff on *.snap empty). cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib tui: 144 passed; --test boundary_readouts: 6 passed. (2) Source scans fail closed, mutated by me and restored: a planted src/tui/planted.rs holding Command::new fails the_tui_source_reads_every_production_module (left: ["planted.rs"]); 'pub(super) mod footer;' in the root panics no_rust_readout_reads_the_model_cell_outside_the_pair_helper ('form the pin does not read'); a fleet_tests.rs declared-free file is refused (left: ["fleet_tests.rs"]); source() unwraps a missing module file. Tree clean after. (3) Seams, not line counts: the commit's module table matches the module docs and the root's ordering; ratchet files ('file size holds'), clones ('duplication holds') and baselines 5eda13bf ('no baseline raised') clean; cargo fmt --check, clippy -p brokkr-cli --all-targets -D warnings, typos --hidden clean. Surviving finding, LOW, author adversarial, 0071 ruling 4 carried under ruling 10 with the implementer's stated reason: crates/brokkr-cli/src/tui/terminal.rs:246 start keeps 11 parameters over the 7-parameter ceiling under its reason-named #[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)]; the signature is byte-identical to the old tui.rs, so this is a moved function the ratchet pairs as new at its new file, not a new breach. Observed, not carried: Tui's struct_excessive_bools at state.rs:125 (no bools ceiling in ruling 4). Process note: two commits where the commission described one; the second closes the parent panel's medium and records its compiling mutation. No security residual, no spec defect, no fail-open path, no weakened refusal. I changed no files and committed nothing.
